# Homa

> You can start with what you already know about your child. Homa helps with planning, printable materials, records, and useful next steps.

URL: https://thankshoma.com
Canonical expanded summary: https://thankshoma.com/llms-full.txt

## What Homa does

Homa helps a parent see what a child does comfortably and what they are learning now. It can create printable materials, record school hours, and save useful family context.

The progress report covers ages 2 to 16. A parent answers questions about things they have seen their child do. The report compares those answers with cited national sources. It shows what looks solid, what is growing, and one useful next step.

A separate state section summarizes reviewed homeschool-law sources and shows when they were last checked. It is not legal advice and cannot confirm that a family has met a legal requirement.

## Current boundaries

- Homa is parent-facing. There is no child account or child-facing AI chat.
- A parent may choose to try optional follow-up questions together with a child.
- Homa can record school hours. It cannot confirm that a family has met a legal requirement.
- A parent can save the name of a curriculum. Current plans do not follow every curriculum's full scope and sequence.
- The planner does not move unfinished activities to new days automatically.
- The progress report remains free under current product policy. The live site is the source for current access and membership details.

## Progress report

Start or return to onboarding: https://thankshoma.com/onboarding

Completion time varies by child and by whether the parent chooses optional follow-up questions. Sample report: https://thankshoma.com/onboarding/sample
Method and sources: https://thankshoma.com/onboarding/method
